newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People News.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Jean & Montamarin's latest campaign for Corona beer, which was unknown in France just five years ago, avoids the usual Mexican stereotypes of sombreros and cactuses and focuses instead on images suggesting the beer should be drunk with a twist of lime. (Reuter)
PARIS - Radio France says it has picked CLM/BBDO to run advertising campaigns for its various stations after several years of working with Publicis.(Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says its board has approved a stake swap with German media mogul Leo Kirch.(Reuter)
PARIS - France says it welcomes an appeal by U.S. President Bill Clinton for a laissez-faire policy on Internet commerce, but says young people and consumers should be protected.(Reuter)

LOS ANGELES - Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros concludes a deal with Spain's Sogecable to provide Sogecable's Canalsatellite, a unit of France's Canal Plus, with pay television, pay-per-view and near video on demand feature films.(Reuter)
PARIS - Summer on French television means endless repeats and no original series in the prime-time evening viewing slot on France's two leading general channels, TF1 and France 2. (Le Parisien)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton proposes to blend its wine and spirits businesses with those of British companies Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc in an independent, listed company.(Reuter)
PARIS - French junior industry minister Christian Pierret attacks a car incentive scheme set up by the previous conservative government for artificially boosting sales.(Reuter)
PARIS - The number of subscribers to mobile phone services in France grew by 6.3 percent in May to 3.27 million, the telecommunications authority ART says in a monthly report on the sector.(Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
